description: How the eVTOL SPAC mania of 2020–2021 turned a cluster of startups into multi‑billion dollar stories — then slammed them into reality. One company fights back; others get ground‑looped.
youtube_description:
The Flying Car Bubble — a chart race through the eVTOL SPAC frenzy and aftermath.

Story: Between 2020 and 2021 venture capital and SPAC money turned startups like Joby, Archer, Lilium and Vertical into household valuations overnight. The chart shows the same boom, then the brutal tidy‑up: certification delays, engineering hurdles, rising interest rates and a capital winter that chopped billions off paper values. Meanwhile EHang — the China‑based drone/AAV play — rode a different path and slowly clawed back value.

Why this matters: eVTOLs promised a new mode of transport. What actually happened is a case study in hype vs. engineering timelines, and how public markets punish missed deadlines.

What to watch in the video: the 2021 SPAC peak, the 2022–2023 crash, and the late emergent winner that surges toward commercialization.
